title: The Captured Internet
targetDuration: 1–2 minutes; hard maximum 120 seconds after measured voice timing

scenes.title: The network works, the public loses
scenes.viewerPurpose: Technical success can coexist with lost control. Diagnoses platform capture through unresolved needs for identity, moderation, discovery and governance, rather than a simple fall from innocent openness.
scenes.composition: A community works smoothly inside a service while its rule-change control sits beyond their reach. Use one strong scene title, flat uncluttered backgrounds, and enough quiet space for the current caption.
addOrChange: A community works smoothly inside a service while its rule-change control sits beyond their reach.
Keep memory, participants and shared work visible around the service’s policy boundary.

cues.text: The internet can work beautifully while the communities inside it lose the power to question its rules.
cues.visualAction: A community works smoothly inside a service while its rule-change control sits beyond their reach.
cues.emotion: Quiet concern; gently emphasize “question its rules”. Let the sentence land in an ordinary speaking voice, with no dramatic swell.

cues.text: The Captured Internet argues that useful services became governing powers when communities could no longer challenge their rules.
cues.visualAction: Keep memory, participants and shared work visible around the service’s policy boundary.
cues.emotion: Clear and warmly interested; give a small emphasis to “challenge their rules”, then finish at an ordinary conversational pace without a dramatic rise.
